name: AI-assisted coding habits
blurb: From vibe coding to developer: habits for working with an AI pair, many drawn from building Argus.

cards.prompt: Why read the diff before accepting an AI's change?
cards.answer: So you understand every line that enters your code: you catch bugs, unwanted side effects and security problems, and you can explain and maintain it later.
Each commit is one understandable change with a clear message, so it is easy to review, to find what broke something, and to undo one change without losing others.

cards.prompt: What does a test give you when an AI writes the code?
cards.answer: An objective check that the code does what you asked, which keeps working after later changes, so you don't rely on the AI saying it works.

cards.prompt: Argus 4.1: how does the server stop other websites from freezing your tasks?
cards.answer: Actions must be JSON (a plain HTML form can't send that), and the browser's Sec-Fetch-Site / Origin headers must show the request came from the Argus page itself.

points.idea: forms from other sites can't do it

cards.prompt: Why escape text before putting it into a page?
cards.answer: Text from outside (descriptions, user input) could contain HTML or script; escaping makes it display as plain text instead of running, preventing injection (XSS).

cards.prompt: Where should passwords and API keys live, and where never?
cards.answer: In a local secrets store or environment variables outside the repository; never committed to git or pasted into code, because git history keeps them forever.

cards.prompt: What makes a good request to an AI coding assistant?
cards.answer: Clear goal, the relevant context (files, constraints, conventions), what done looks like, and asking it to explain or test its change.

cards.prompt: Why ask the AI to explain code before changing it?
cards.answer: Explaining surfaces wrong assumptions early and builds your own understanding, so the change you approve fits how the code really works.
Reproduce it reliably and read the actual error or log, before guessing at fixes.
